entries.notes_md:
- **Installing from Windows also keeps the screen resolution** when Windows was set below the screen's largest, such as a 4K TV run at 1080p.
- **A newly installed display can read its own update settings**, so its update channel is reported correctly from the start.
- **Installing is about a minute quicker**, and the boot-splash step is shown once.

- **Installing from Windows keeps the screen's orientation**, so a portrait screen comes up portrait instead of needing to be rotated by hand.
- **Remote support shows the real screen on every display**; on some it showed a black screen.

- **The installer asks which updates the display should follow: Stable (recommended) or Testing.** Both the USB installer and the install from Windows ask.
- **Remote support recovers by itself on a new install**, instead of needing its service restarted by hand.

- **A new display checks for updates before it shows the setup screen**, so it starts on current software.
- **The remote-support agent is restarted once after the first boot**, so it comes online on its own after an install.
- **A newly installed display enrols for remote support within a minute or two** (it retried every ten minutes).

- **Graphics firmware for AMD processors**, so machines with AMD graphics display correctly.
- **First-boot services** that check for updates and enrol the display for remote support as soon as it is installed.
- **The display keeps a named “SteadyScreen” entry in the computer's boot menu**, instead of a generic “UEFI OS” entry, so it can be picked out in the firmware menu.

- **The mouse pointer hides after five seconds of not moving.**
- **Settings chosen during installation are kept**; some were being written where the finished system could not see them.
- **The boot splash no longer resets on every boot.**

- **Newer Linux kernel (6.12.107).**
- **The installer applies the latest software staged with it**, so a new display comes up current instead of on the software the image was built with.
- **The admin page is on the standard web port (80)** on a fresh install; it no longer comes up on 8080.

- **Network printers found on the local network can be added reliably.** A discovered printer is now attached by its address, because the system could find printers on the network but could not always reach them by name.
